doctor.definition: Children take the roles of physician or patient or nurse and pretend they are at the physician's office.

nurse.definition: A trained healthcare worker who cares for patients and supports treatment.

surgeon.definition: A physician who specializes in surgery.

paramedic.definition: A person trained to assist medical professionals and to give emergency medical treatment.

receptionist.definition: A secretary whose main duty is to answer the telephone and receive visitors.

pharmacist.definition: A health professional trained in the art of preparing and dispensing drugs.

anesthesiologist.definition: A specialist who administers an anesthetic to a patient before they are treated.

radiologist.definition: A doctor who interprets medical images to help diagnose or treat conditions.

pediatrician.definition: A doctor who cares for infants, children, and young people.

psychiatrist.definition: A physician who specializes in psychiatry.

midwife.definition: A woman skilled in aiding the delivery of babies.

orderly.definition: A hospital worker who helps move patients and supports everyday ward tasks.

ophthalmologist.definition: A medical doctor specializing in the diagnosis and treatment of diseases of the eye.

dermatologist.definition: A doctor who specializes in the physiology and pathology of the skin.

neurologist.definition: A medical specialist in the nervous system and the disorders affecting it.

orthopedist.definition: A doctor who treats problems affecting bones, joints, and muscles.

ent-specialist.definition: A doctor specializing in conditions of the ear, nose, and throat, also called an otolaryngologist.
ent-specialist.exampleUsage: The patient was referred to an ENT specialist.

urologist.definition: A doctor who treats conditions of the urinary system.

oncologist.definition: A doctor who specializes in diagnosing and treating cancer.

gastroenterologist.definition: A physician who specializes in diseases of the gastrointestinal tract.

pulmonologist.definition: A doctor specializing in diseases and conditions of the lungs and respiratory system.
pulmonologist.exampleUsage: The pulmonologist reviewed the breathing tests.

physiotherapist.definition: Therapist who treats injury or dysfunction with exercises and other physical treatments of the disorder.

dietitian.definition: A specialist in the study of diet and nutrition.

lab-technician.definition: A trained technical worker who prepares materials, operates laboratory instruments, conducts routine tests, and records findings under scientists’ or senior staff’s supervision.
lab-technician.exampleUsage: The lab technician was used during the activity.

emt.definition: A trained worker who gives emergency medical care before a patient reaches hospital.

emergency-room.definition: A hospital or clinic area is prepared and staffed to treat people who need medical attention immediately.

waiting-room.definition: A room where patients or visitors sit until they are called.
waiting-room.exampleUsage: Patients waited in the waiting room.

operating-room.definition: A specially equipped hospital room is used for surgery and kept sterile to reduce the risk of infection.

recovery-room.definition: A hospital room where patients are monitored and cared for after surgery.

patient-room.definition: A hospital room where a patient stays for care, observation, or recovery.
patient-room.exampleUsage: The patient room had a call button beside the bed.

intensive-care-unit.definition: A hospital unit providing continuous monitoring and advanced care for critically ill or injured patients.
intensive-care-unit.exampleUsage: The intensive-care unit is staffed for continuous critical care.

maternity-ward.definition: A hospital ward where women receive care during pregnancy and childbirth, alongside care for their newborn infants.

nursery.definition: A hospital area where newborn babies receive care.

laboratory.definition: A region resembling a laboratory inasmuch as it offers opportunities for observation and practice and experimentation.

radiology.definition: The medical field that uses imaging to help diagnose and treat conditions.

cafeteria.definition: A restaurant where you serve yourself and pay a cashier.

pharmacy.definition: A retail shop where medicine and other articles are sold.

consulting-room.definition: A private room where a doctor or other healthcare professional meets and examines patients.
consulting-room.exampleUsage: The doctor spoke with the patient in the consulting room.

triage-area.definition: An emergency-care area where trained staff assess patients and prioritize care according to urgency.
triage-area.exampleUsage: The triage area is used to assess how urgently patients need care.

burn-unit.definition: A specialized hospital unit for patients with serious burn injuries.
burn-unit.exampleUsage: The burn unit provides specialized multidisciplinary care.

dialysis-unit.definition: A hospital or clinic unit where dialysis treatment is provided to patients with kidney failure or related conditions.
dialysis-unit.exampleUsage: The dialysis unit contains specialized treatment equipment.

isolation-room.definition: A hospital room used to separate a patient who may have, or has, an illness that can spread.

sterilization-room.definition: A controlled area where reusable medical instruments are cleaned, packaged, and sterilized.
sterilization-room.exampleUsage: Sterile instruments were prepared in the sterilization room.

rehabilitation-room.definition: A room used for supervised therapy that helps patients regain movement, strength, or daily-living skills.
rehabilitation-room.exampleUsage: The patient attended a supervised session in the rehabilitation room.

blood-bank.definition: A reserve of donated blood units is kept at a hospital or blood center for transfusions.

stethoscope.definition: A medical instrument for listening to the sounds generated inside the body.
stethoscope.exampleUsage: The stethoscope was used during the activity.

syringe.definition: To spray or irrigate (a body part) with a syringe.

thermometer.exampleUsage: The thermometer was used during the activity.

blood-pressure-monitor.definition: A device used to measure and display blood pressure.
blood-pressure-monitor.exampleUsage: The nurse used a blood-pressure monitor during the assessment.

iv-drip.definition: A system that delivers prescribed fluids or medicines into a vein through intravenous tubing under clinical supervision.
iv-drip.exampleUsage: The IV drip was monitored by qualified clinical staff.

wheelchair.definition: A movable chair mounted on large wheels.

stretcher.definition: A flat support used to carry a person who cannot walk safely.

oxygen-mask.definition: A device worn over the nose and mouth delivers oxygen from a connected storage tank.
oxygen-mask.exampleUsage: The oxygen mask was used during the activity.

defibrillator.definition: A device that gives an electric shock to help restore a normal heart rhythm.
defibrillator.exampleUsage: The defibrillator was used during the activity.

scalpel.definition: A thin straight surgical knife used in dissection and surgery.
scalpel.exampleUsage: The glossary uses the term "scalpel" in an educational description.

bandage.definition: To dress by covering or binding.

cast.definition: Container into which liquid is poured to create a given shape when it hardens.

ventilator.definition: A medical machine that helps a patient breathe.
ventilator.exampleUsage: The ventilator was used during the activity.

catheter.definition: A thin flexible tube inserted into the body to permit introduction or withdrawal of fluids or to keep the passageway open.

pulse-oximeter.definition: A noninvasive device that estimates blood oxygen saturation and pulse rate, usually from a fingertip.
pulse-oximeter.exampleUsage: The nurse checked the pulse oximeter reading.

ecg-machine.definition: A machine that records the heart's electrical activity as an electrocardiogram.
ecg-machine.exampleUsage: The ECG machine recorded the heart rhythm.

nebulizer.definition: A device that turns liquid medicine into a mist for breathing in.

tourniquet.definition: Bandage that stops the flow of blood from an artery by applying pressure.

surgical-mask.definition: A disposable medical mask designed to reduce the spread of droplets and protect a clinical field from contamination.
surgical-mask.exampleUsage: Clinical staff wore surgical masks according to infection-control policy.

reflex-hammer.definition: A small medical instrument used by clinicians to test tendon reflexes.
reflex-hammer.exampleUsage: The doctor used a reflex hammer during the neurological examination.

heart.definition: The hollow muscular organ located behind the sternum and between the lungs.

lungs.definition: Either of two saclike respiratory organs in the chest of vertebrates.

brain.definition: That which is responsible for one's thoughts, feelings, and conscious brain functions.

bone.definition: A hard part of the skeleton that supports and protects the body.

blood.definition: The fluid (red in vertebrates) that is pumped through the body by the heart and contains plasma, blood cells, and platelets.

pulse.definition: The rhythmic contraction and expansion of the arteries with each beat of the heart.

fever.definition: A rise in the temperature of the body.

infection.definition: (medicine) the invasion of the body by pathogenic microorganisms and their multiplication which can lead to tissue damage and disease.

injury.definition: Any physical damage to the body caused by violence or accident or fracture etc.

fracture.definition: Breaking of hard tissue such as bone.

allergy.definition: Hypersensitivity reaction to a particular allergen.

rash.definition: A series of unexpected and unpleasant occurrences.

liver.definition: Large and complicated reddish-brown glandular organ located in the upper right portion of the abdominal cavity.

kidneys.definition: Either of two bean-shaped excretory organs that filter wastes (especially urea) from the blood and excrete them and water in urine.

spine.definition: The part of a book's cover that encloses the inner side of the book's pages and that faces outward when the book is shelved.

stomach.definition: The digestive organ that receives food and begins breaking it down.

intestines.definition: The part of the alimentary canal between the stomach and the anus.

muscles.definition: One of the contractile organs of the body.

arteries.definition: Blood vessels that carry blood away from the heart to tissues throughout the body.
arteries.exampleUsage: Arteries carry blood away from the heart.

appendix.definition: A small pouch connected to the beginning of the large intestine.

inflammation.definition: The body's response to injury or infection, often causing redness, warmth, swelling, or pain.

examination.definition: A healthcare professional's check of a person's body or health.

diagnosis.definition: Identification of a health condition from its signs, symptoms, and test results.

prescription.definition: A drug that is available only with written instructions from a doctor or dentist to a pharmacist.

surgery.definition: A room in a hospital equipped for the performance of surgical operations.

x-ray.definition: High-energy electromagnetic radiation, carried in extremely short waves, can pass through many materials for medical imaging, security screening, and scientific analysis.

blood-test.definition: Analysis of a blood sample can reveal, measure, or track substances, cells, and other signs of how the body is working.

injection.definition: The act of putting a liquid into the body by means of a syringe.

vaccination.definition: Taking a vaccine as a precaution against contracting a disease.

mri-scan.definition: A diagnostic imaging examination that uses strong magnetic fields and radio waves to create detailed images inside the body.
mri-scan.exampleUsage: The doctor reviewed the MRI scan.

stitches.definition: Sutures used by healthcare professionals to close surgical cuts or wounds.
stitches.exampleUsage: The nurse checked the stitches during follow-up care.

physical-therapy.definition: A health care discipline that assesses movement problems and treats them with exercise, hands-on techniques, and other physical methods.

biopsy.definition: Examination of tissues or liquids from the living body to determine the existence or cause of a disease.

dialysis.definition: A treatment that removes waste and extra fluid when the kidneys cannot do so adequately.

transfusion.definition: The introduction of blood or blood plasma into a vein or artery.

chemotherapy.definition: Treatment using drugs to destroy cancer cells or stop their growth.

endoscopy.definition: Visual examination of the interior of a hollow body organ by use of an endoscope.

ct-scan.definition: A medical examination that uses X-rays to produce detailed images inside the body.

colonoscopy.definition: Visual examination of the colon (with a colonoscope) from the cecum to the rectum.

transplant.definition: (surgery) tissue or organ transplanted from a donor to a recipient.

hospital-bed.definition: An adjustable bed used to care for patients.

pillow.definition: A soft rectangular pad that supports your head while you sleep.

blanket.definition: A thick woven cover, often wool, laid over you for warmth.

gown.definition: The members of a university as distinguished from the other residents of the town in which the university is located.

chart.definition: A record of a patient's medical information and treatment.

clipboard.definition: A small writing board with a clip at the top for holding papers.

medicine.definition: A substance used to prevent, treat, or relieve illness.

pills.definition: Small solid doses of medicine that are usually swallowed.

ointment.definition: Semisolid preparation (usually containing a medicine) applied externally as a remedy or for soothing an irritation.

crutches.definition: Mobility aids used to support body weight and assist walking when a leg or foot cannot bear normal weight.
crutches.exampleUsage: The physiotherapist adjusted the crutches for the patient.

walker.definition: A frame that helps someone stay steady while walking.

ambulance.definition: A vehicle that takes people to and from hospitals.

face-shield.definition: A clear protective covering worn over the face.

hand-sanitizer.definition: A liquid or gel used to clean your hands when soap and water are unavailable.

sharps-container.definition: A puncture-resistant approved container for disposing of needles and other sharp medical items.
sharps-container.exampleUsage: Used sharps were placed in the approved sharps container.

bedpan.definition: A shallow vessel used by a bedridden patient for defecation and urination.

patient-wristband.definition: A hospital identification band worn by a patient and used to confirm important identity information.
patient-wristband.exampleUsage: Staff checked the patient wristband before care.

call-button.definition: A bedside button that allows a hospital patient to call nursing or care staff for assistance.
call-button.exampleUsage: The patient used the call button to request help.

iv-pole.definition: A tall wheeled stand used to hold intravenous fluid bags and related equipment.
iv-pole.exampleUsage: The IV pole stood beside the bed.

oxygen-tank.definition: A high-pressure cylinder containing medical oxygen for use by trained or authorized healthcare personnel.
oxygen-tank.exampleUsage: The oxygen tank was secured according to hospital safety procedures.
